title: Quadratic model — finding a maximum
problem: A ball is thrown upward. Its height $h$ (metres) at time $t$ (seconds) is $h = -5t^2 + 20t$. Find (a) the height at $t = 1$ s and (b) the maximum height.

steps.instruction: Part (a): substitute $t = 1$ into the height equation.
Part (b): for a quadratic $h = at^2 + bt + c$, the maximum (when $a < 0$) occurs at $t = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$.
Substitute $t = 2$ to find the maximum height.

answer: (a) The height at $t = 1$ s is 15 m. (b) The maximum height is 20 m, reached at 2 seconds.

title: Exponential model — growth and decay
problem: A car purchased for \$30\,000 depreciates at 15% per year. Its value after $t$ years is $V = 30\,000 \times (0.85)^t$. (a) Find the value after 4 years. (b) After how many years is the car worth less than \$10\,000?

steps.instruction: Part (a): substitute $t = 4$ into the value equation.
Part (b): try successive values of $t$ to find when the value first drops below \$10\,000.

answer: (a) The value after 4 years is approximately \$15\,660.19. (b) The car is first worth less than \$10\,000 in year 7.

title: Reciprocal model
problem: The time $t$ (hours) to complete a job varies inversely with the number of workers $n$: $t = \dfrac{24}{n}$. (a) How long does the job take with 6 workers? (b) How many workers are needed to complete it in 3 hours?

steps.instruction: Describe the key feature of reciprocal graphs.
steps.working: As $n$ increases, $t$ decreases — but never reaches zero. As $n$ decreases toward zero, $t$ grows without bound. The graph has horizontal and vertical asymptotes at $t = 0$ and $n = 0$.

answer: (a) With 6 workers, the job takes 4 hours. (b) 8 workers are needed to finish in 3 hours.
